data.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 21 at 11:58PM EDT until October 24 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
data.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

FXUS62 KMFL 221130
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
730 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

...New UPDATE, AVIATION, BEACHES...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 730 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

 - Hazardous marine conditions continue through the end of the
   work week for the Atlantic waters. Hazardous winds and seas for
   all local waters return this weekend.
 
 - High risk of rip currents continues for the Atlantic beaches,
   and will likely last at least into early next week. In
   addition, high surf conditions continue for the Palm Beaches.

 - Moderate coastal flooding is expected to continue around high 
   tide along the east coast. A low, 10-30% chance of major 
   coastal flooding is possible beginning during the second half 
   of the upcoming weekend.

 - Heavy rain, isolated flash flooding, and windy conditions are
   forecast for this weekend into early next week.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 730 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Low-level trough just north of the Bahamas, embedded in the 
general N-NE wind flow, is skirting the Florida east coast this 
morning and helping to trigger scattered showers along and 
offshore the Palm Beach County coast. Hi-res/short range models
are handling this scenario fairly well, and depict a southward
spread of the showers mainly over the nearshore Atlantic waters
but skirting the east coast metro from time to time through much
of the day. Current forecast PoPs are handling this well so no
changes needed to the forecast at this time except to increase
cloud cover southward along the east coast this morning. 

NOS tide gauges are peaking in the minor flood stage at the
current high tide, except bordering on moderate at Lake Worth
Pier. These levels continue slightly above guidance, so current
expectation of moderate flood levels with upcoming high tides over
the next several days is on track.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Friday)
Issued at 106 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Latest surface analysis shows high pressure over the TN Valley, and 
Subtropical Storm Josephine off the New England coast. At the upper 
levels, the ridge over the center of the country continues to nose 
eastward and a trough is slowly deepening over the eastern third of 
the country. Latest 00Z sounding shows plenty of dry air at the mid 
and upper levels, with some low level moisture to support widely 
scattered coastal showers today. Winds will continue to be out of 
the NNE and gusting to around 20-25 mph this afternoon. High temps 
will be in the low to middle 80s. Scattered coastal showers will 
continue overnight with mainly dry conditions over the interior and 
SW FL. Overnight lows will be comfortable ranging from the low to 
mid 60s around the lake region, the lower 70s closer to the coast. 

As the trough continues to deepen on Friday and an upper low starts 
to develop off the SE US coast late in the day, low level moisture 
will start to increase with PWAT values nosing up to around 1.5 
inches. Forecast soundings still show plenty of dry air aloft, but 
the shower activity should be more increased across the east coast 
metro compared to the past several days. Could even see some 
isolated thunderstorms near the coast. NE winds will be pick up a 
bit on Friday, with wind gusts of 20-30 mph possible, especially 
along the coast. Afternoon high temps will again be in the low to 
middle 80s.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Friday night through Wednesday)
Issued at 106 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

As we head into the weekend and into early next week, a multi hazard 
event will be taking shape as an upper level low lingers in the 
region and strong surface high pressure builds into the eastern US. 
Enhanced moisture around the upper low will bring rounds of showers, 
heavy at times, to SE FL from Saturday through Monday. While mean 
QPF values have trended downward the past several days, 1-3 inches 
is still expected across the east coast metro, with localized higher 
end amounts of 4-6 inches possible. This rain combined with the 
higher king tides this weekend may present some flooding issues. WPC 
has a Slight risk of excessive rain across the metro both days this 
weekend. The other main story will be the gusty winds this weekend 
as the pressure gradient tightens. NE winds will gust 25-35 mph on 
Saturday and 30-40 mph on Sunday. 

Conditions begin to improve Tuesday into mid week as the upper low 
pulls away from the region to the northeast and with it the deeper 
moisture will exit the area. There will still be scattered coastal 
showers around both days, but the rainfall flooding threat will 
decrease. 

Fairly comfortable temperatures are expected this weekend into next 
week with high temps generally in the low to middle 80s, and low 
temps each day in the 60s/70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 730 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

VFR conditions expected through the forecast period with a
predominant BKN occasionally OVC layer 050-060. SHRA over the 
nearshore Atlantic waters will skirt the east coast and could 
briefly affect some of the terminals for much of the period. Main 
impact will be brief MVFR ceiling/visibility, primarily at KDJT
through about 14z, with lower confidence at the remainder of the
terminals where VCSH is indicated. Wind 330-350 degrees near 10 
knots through 15z-17z, becoming 020-030 degrees after 17z. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 106 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Hazardous seas will continue in the Atlantic waters the rest of the 
week with seas of 5-8 ft. NE winds 15-20 kts through Friday for all 
local waters. 

Hazardous winds and seas return for all local waters this weekend 
into early next week as the pressure gradient tightens across the 
area. Gale force winds are possible in both the Atlantic and Gulf 
waters this weekend. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Issued at 106 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

We're beginning to come out of an ebb in the astronomical tides 
as we head towards the full moon and peak of the tide forecasts 
late this weekend and into early next week. Observed water-levels 
are already over-performing predictions and we'll likely begin 
reaching Moderate flooding thresholds this evening at all of our 
east coast tidal stations. It's also not out of the question that
Palm Beach county may even reach Major flooding levels at the 
peak of the King Tide. 

The normal King Tides are complicated by the fact that we'll be 
dealing with a complex upper/surface low pressure pattern that 
will feature an approaching front from the north and convection 
rising out of the Caribbean from the south. This will likely 
increase the onshore wind component and magnify the already high 
tides. This is somewhat accounted for in the predictions mentioned
above, but only crudely. Furthermore, the potential for heavy 
rainfall during periods of high tide is also something to be aware
of that could further aggravate coastal flooding. In short, we're
heading into what could be a rather impactful period for coastal 
flooding and sensitive locations should consider preparations.

&&

TWOAT 

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Subtropical 
Storm Josephine, located a few hundred miles offshore of the 
Mid-Atlantic coast of the United States.

Subtropical Central Atlantic:
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles to the 
east-southeast of Bermuda is producing a large area of disorganized 
showers and thunderstorms. Some development of this system is 
possible during the next day or two while it moves slowly 
north-northeastward. Upper-level winds are forecast to become too 
strong for further development by the weekend.  
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Josephine are issued under WMO header WTNT35 
KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT5.
Forecast/Advisories on Josephine are issued under WMO header WTNT25 
KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT5.

$$
